log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P1's side
Stealth Rock up on P1's side
Toxic Spikes up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper and Swampert to immediately set up rain via Drizzle and Mega Evolve Swampert for Swift Swim speed control and offensive pressure against their sun/balanced core. Bring Whimsicott in the back for Tailwind backup and Prankster utility, and Basculegion to clean up with Choice Scarf Adaptability.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead Pelipper + Swampert, back Whimsicott + Basculegion.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex and Skarmory lead to absorb rain-boosted Water/Ground pressure while setting Toxic Spikes and dual hazards (Stealth Rock + Spikes). Aegislash backs up as the dedicated Mega Ampharos and special-attacker switch-in with 202 SpD and Expert Belt leverage. Meowscarada with Choice Scarf at 190 Speed provides late-game cleaning and revenge-kills the opponent's fast special attackers (Whimsicott, Basculegion).
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. My Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Prioritize hazard stacking from Skarmory to wear down the rain team over repeated switches. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf makes it the win condition once hazards are up.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper targets Skarmory with Hurricane while Swampert targets Toxapex with Liquidation without Mega Evolving yet, keeping matchup options flexible against Skarmory and Toxapex.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Lead Pelipper + Swampert against Toxapex + Skarmory in rain.

decisions.rationale: Stacking Toxic Spikes + Spikes on Turn 1 maximizes chip damage on the rain team's frequent switch-ins, directly executing the hazard-wear-down plan to enable Meowscarada as the late-game win condition.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Pelipper) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Pelipper targets Skarmory with Hydro Pump for a guaranteed KO through its remaining 67% HP, while Mega Swampert uses Earthquake with Mega Evolve to hit both opponents (doing heavy damage to Toxapex and pressuring the board while immune to Skarmory).
decisions.notebook: Swampert has Swampertite and can Mega Evolve for Swift Swim speed boost in rain. Pelipper holds Damp Rock.

decisions.rationale: Baneful Bunker (priority +4) shields Toxapex from Swampert's Earthquake and poisons on contact, preserving its longevity. Stealth Rock is the highest-value hazard to set against a rain squad—Water and Flying switch-ins take 25% chip, accelerating the wear-down plan before Meowscarada sweeps.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. My Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Prioritize hazard stacking from Skarmory to wear down the rain team over repeated switches. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf makes it the win condition once hazards are up. Stealth Rock not yet on either side—critical to set now.

decisions.rationale: Meowscarada with Choice Scarf (Speed 190 → ~285) outspeeds both opponent's Pelipper (85–117) and Swift Swim Swampert-Mega (180–244), letting it strike first with super-effective LeafStorm on Swampert-Mega to threaten a KO and remove the biggest offensive threat. Toxapex should pass and stay in to remain as a defensive wall, keeping Toxic Spikes pressure while Meowscarada executes the win condition.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Stealth Rock is now on the opponent's side via Skarmory—critical advantage. Continue stacking hazards; Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf is the win condition once hazards wear down the foe.

decisions.rationale: Meowscarada outspeeds our whole team due to Choice Scarf (effective Speed 235-288 vs Mega Swampert's 180). Pelipper targets Meowscarada with Hurricane for a super-effective hit, while Mega Swampert targets Meowscarada with Liquidation (or we can hit Toxapex with Earthquake, but Meowscarada threatens Swampert severely with Grass moves). However, Meowscarada resists Earthquake and is weak to Ice. Let's use Pelipper's Hurricane into Meowscarada and Swampert's Ice Punch into Meowscarada to secure a KO on the dangerous Choice Scarf Meowscarada.
decisions.notebook: Meowscarada runs Choice Scarf making it faster than Swift Swim Swampert. Toxapex holds Rindo Berry and can use Baneful Bunker or Recover.

decisions.rationale: Swampert fainted last turn, so we must replace it. Basculegion enters in rain with Choice Scarf and Adaptability to clean up remaining threats, while Pelipper maintains board position.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Meowscarada was choice-scarfed. Toxapex holds Rindo Berry and has Regenerator. Basculegion is a strong late-game cleaner under rain.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex uses Recover to fully heal back to 100% HP, maintaining its role as the defensive backbone against the rain core's physical threats. Meowscarada uses Leaf Storm targeting Swampert-Mega for the 4x super-effective hit (Grass vs Water/Ground), aiming to eliminate the opponent's most dangerous attacker and Mega Evolution outright. Even accounting for Leaf Storm's -2 SpA drawback, removing Mega Swampert significantly weakens the opposing rain team and accelerates Meowscarada's sweep path.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory—critical advantage. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf is the win condition once hazards wear down the foe. Prioritize eliminating Mega Swampert to break the rain offensive core.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Pelipper targets Aegislash with Hurricane to pressure it, while Choice Scarf Basculegion hits Aegislash with Last Respects for super-effective damage (Aegislash is Ghost/Steel).
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Toxapex and Aegislash remaining. Basculegion's Last Respects is very strong against Aegislash.

decisions.rationale: Baneful Bunker protects Toxapex from Basculegion's Water coverage (FlipTurn/WaveCrash, both not very effective) and poisons any contact attacker. King's Shield protects Aegislash from Basculegion's super-effective Ghost moves (PhantomForce/LastRespects) and drops Basculegion's Attack by two stages, crippling its physical damage for the rest of the game. Both moves have +4 priority, ensuring they execute before Basculegion's Choice Scarf speed advantage. This preserves Aegislash as the essential Mega Ampharos answer and lets Basculegion's poison plus hazard chip finish it off over subsequent turns.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory—critical advantage. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf is the win condition once hazards wear down the foe. Prioritize eliminating Mega Swampert to break the rain offensive core. Mega Swampert is now eliminated; next priority is neutralizing Basculegion's Choice Scarf threat and preserving Aegislash for the Mega Ampharos matchup.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper stays in and uses Hurricane into Aegislash, while Basculegion switches out to Whimsicott to reset its Choice lock and avoid King's Shield penalty.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion can switch out via Whimsicott to reset Choice lock.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex layers Toxic Spikes to pressure future foe switch-ins. Aegislash uses Shadow Ball on Basculegion: it is super-effective (2x) and Basculegion is at 63% HP, giving a real chance to outright KO the Choice-Scarfed threat. Even if it doesn't KO, Aegislash at 100% HP survives Last Respects (max 55% damage) and can finish Basculegion next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf is the win condition once hazards wear down the foe. Mega Swampert eliminated. Basculegion is Choice-locked into Last Respects. Prioritize removing Basculegion then pivot to the Mega Ampharos matchup.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper uses Hurricane on Aegislash-Blade (which caused confusion last turn and is vulnerable), while Whimsicott sets Tailwind to secure the speed advantage and offensive presence for the rest of the game.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion is available in the back; Choice lock can be reset via Whimsicott switching if needed.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex stacks Toxic Spikes to upgrade switch-in poison to toxic for Basculegion and other foes; Aegislash uses King's Shield to safely block Pelipper's Hurricane, preserve its 82% HP for the Basculegion switch-in, and prepare to block Last Respects next turn.

Aegislash is currently confused and slower under Tailwind, and we can switch Whimsicott out to Basculegion while Pelipper hits Aegislash with Hurricane to pressure past its Ghost/Steel typing. Basculegion can then enter safely to clean up.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion is ready in the back; keep track of Aegislash King's Shield and Toxapex Regenerator.

decisions.rationale: Baneful Bunker protects Toxapex (full HP) from Whimsicott's likely Moonblast and scouts opponent intent; King's Shield is the safest Aegislash option given confusion—its +4 priority blocks Pelipper's guaranteed Hurricane before Whimsicott can act, preserving Aegislash's 82% HP for the critical Basculegion matchup next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent runs rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert eliminated, Basculegion) backed by Mega Ampharos as special breaker. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Aegislash is the key Mega Ampharos answer. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory. Meowscarada's Protean + Scarf is the win condition once hazards wear down the foe. Prioritize removing Basculegion then pivot to Mega Ampharos. Basculegion is Choice-locked into Last Respects.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper targets Aegislash with Hurricane while Basculegion uses Last Respects on Aegislash. This double-targets Aegislash to break through King's Shield / damage it while ignoring Toxapex's Rindo Berry and Baneful Bunker/Recover loops. Tailwind is active so we outspeed, and Rain boosts Water moves or Weather Ball if needed, but Hurricane and Last Respects hit Aegislash effectively.
decisions.notebook: Basculegion Last Respects and Pelipper Hurricane pressure Aegislash effectively while bypassing Toxapex defensive utility.

decisions.rationale: Aegislash Shadow Ball guarantees a KO on Basculegion (26% HP, super-effective, 61.2-111.8% damage range covers target entirely). Aegislash survives both Basculegion's Last Respects (37.7-55.3%) and Pelipper's Hurricane (12.6-18.9%) at 82% HP, ending at roughly 8-32% HP. Removing Basculegion is the stated priority. Toxapex uses Haze as the highest-value safe option—Recover is wasted at full HP, Toxic Spikes are already layered, and Baneful Bunker has reduced success rate with no incoming contact threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain core: Pelipper remains after Basculegion and Whimsicott are eliminated. Next expected pivot is Mega Ampharos—Aegislash is the key answer. Meowscarada is the late-game win condition once hazards wear down. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. After this KO, plan to switch low-HP Aegislash out next turn and pivot to Mega Ampharos.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper uses Hurricane to chunk Toxapex while Basculegion fires off Last Respects. Tailwind expires this turn, so we maximize offensive output.
decisions.notebook: preserve Last Respects and Hurricane pressure against Toxapex in endgame situations.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex sets Toxic Spikes to pressure the opponent's remaining grounded Pokémon (Primarina, Forretress) and support Meowscarada as the late-game win condition; Basculegion is nearly dead from poison and Choice-locked, so hazards will wear down switches. Aegislash is fainted and must Pass.
decisions.notebook: Opponent rain core: Pelipper remains after Basculegion and Whimsicott are eliminated. Next expected pivot is Mega Ampharos—Aegislash is the key answer. Meowscarada is the late-game win condition once hazards wear down. Stealth Rock is on opponent's side via Skarmory. Toxapex carries Rindo Berry for Swampert EQ. Opponent has Primarina and Forretress remaining; both are grounded and will take Toxic Spikes damage on switch-in.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper's Hurricane cleanly KOs Toxapex from 16% (guaranteed). Basculegion uses Last Respects into Toxapex just in case or as a backup, though Hurricane alone finishes it.
decisions.notebook: Maintain awareness of Toxapex's Rindo Berry, Regenerator, and Baneful Bunker options in future games; preserve Pelipper/Basculegion endgame synergy.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex at 16% HP needs immediate recovery to remain an effective defensive wall. Recover brings it to ~90%, allowing it to absorb Pelipper's incoming hits (Hydro Pump is resisted 0.5x, Hurricane is neutral but manageable) while continuing to spread hazards. Basculegion at 1% HP poisoned will almost certainly faint from residual poison before acting, so there is no urgent incoming threat requiring Baneful Bunker's protection this turn. Aegislash is fainted with no other option than Pass.

reflections.summary: The game was won by overwhelming the opponent's defensive setup core (Skarmory, Aegislash, Toxapex) with sustained rain offense from Pelipper and Swampert early, followed by cleaning up with Basculegion's Last Respects once the defensive threats were isolated.
reflections.adjustment: Be mindful of timing protection moves (King's Shield and Baneful Bunker) from the opponent's defensive pivot pieces to avoid wasting attacking turns.
reflections.notebook: Maintain awareness of Toxapex's Rindo Berry, Regenerator, and Baneful Bunker options in future games; preserve Pelipper/Basculegion endgame synergy; respect Aegislash's King's Shield stalling.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because Basculegion's Last Respects snowballed out of control after powering up through multiple KOs, overwhelming my team once Aegislash fell. My hazard advantage (Spikes/Stealth Rock via Skarmory) was negated by opponent's own hazard stack (Spikes + Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes) grinding down Toxapex to 16% before Basculegion delivered the finishing blow. Meowscarada was an ineffective pick—died immediately to Hurricane in Pelipper's rain without contributing meaningfully. I also never Mega Evolved any Pokémon, leaving a Mega Stone slot wasted when the opponent successfully Mega Evolved Swampert for early pressure.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Meowscarada or adjust the fourth slot to include a dedicated Basculegion/Last Respects check—ideally a Pokémon that resists Ghost/Fighting or can threaten Basculegion on the switch (e.g., a Normal-resistant or Fighting-resistant pivot). Additionally, Mega Evolve Aegislash on the turn it predicts a Last Respects or Hurricane, gaining offensive pressure to punish the opponent before Basculegion reaches 3–4 Last Respects uses, or use the Mega slot proactively to break through Pelipper and disrupt rain earlier.
reflections.notebook: Opponent rain core: Pelipper (Drizzle) + Mega Swampert is the offensive foundation; Basculegion (Choice Scarf, Adaptability) with Last Respects is the primary win-condition—power snowballs with each fainted teammate, reached 4 uses by turn 10. Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Prankster) provides Tailwind speed control and disruption; survived to 5% through multiple turns. Opponent hazard-stacked Spikes + Stealth Rock + Toxic Spikes via Skarmory/Forretress. Primarina (Mystic Water, Liquid Voice) and Forretress (Sitrus Berry, Sturdy) remain unpivoted—expect Forretress as a Rapid Spin/Stealth Rock lead or pivot next game. Key lesson: Last Respects requires an immediate answer before turn 6 or it becomes unanswerable. Next game plan: bring a Ghost- or Fighting-resistant pivot, Mega Evolve proactively, and prioritize eliminating Basculegion before it reaches 3+ Last Respects stacks.
